sourceEvidence.label: A90 boot-only F1 owner policy, source, tests, and runtime qualification

assessment.summary: The A90 owner can preserve one-shot F1 safety while removing host-runtime, test, and historical-evidence couplings that slow repeated kernel experiments.

nonNegotiables: one candidate release and one rollback release
fresh serial identity and final health
assumptions: Root and malicious concurrent processes under the invoking UID are outside the lane.
Existing A90 Native serial and TWRP recovery interfaces remain available.
No measured performance or memory budget was supplied.

opportunities.title: Align owner identity with A90 effect authority
opportunities.summary: Keep controls that select or repeat a boot write in the owner closure and move tests, reviews, historical evidence, and broad host runtime state to their correct lifetimes.
opportunities.diagnosis: The current execution identity includes non-executed tests and host runtime inventories and couples independent qualifications to owner code, so harmless drift triggers capability churn before the required crash reconciler exists.

evidence.claim: The binding F1 invariants require exact artifacts, durable journal state, no candidate replay, rollback, and final health.
The owner closure includes its focused test and the owner implements ten-file staging plus four command subprocesses.
Resident, recovery, runtime, and hazard qualifications bind the owner closure.
The focused suite produced 75/76 because host Python runtime inventory drifted while the owner source closure still matched.
The existing helper already owns native serial recovery request, recovery ADB flash/readback, reboot, and serial verification.
Control identity is broader than the components that can select or repeat the A90 boot-write effect.

desiredInvariants: Candidate-only changes alter manifest data without reopening owner capability review.
Tests and review artifacts validate but never participate in the live execution digest.
Only A90 boot may be written, with one candidate and one rollback release.
Recovery ADB is bound only during the recovery transport window.
Every crash prefix resumes from durable journal state without repeating a device effect.

options.title: Correct the current strong closure
options.summary: Retain broad host runtime and staged-source binding while removing tests, owner-bound independent evidence, and pre-bridge ADB ownership.

evidenceCoverage.rationale: The resume table and existing one-shot controls implement the F1 invariants.
Tests leave the closure, but staged source and four command workers remain.
Independent evidence is decoupled from owner code.
Broad host runtime drift remains capability-significant.
The mature helper remains the recovery adapter.

tradeoffs.assessment: Removes false couplings while retaining broad trusted-host byte coverage.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Recompute closure membership and run the existing hostile corpus.

tradeoffs.assessment: Four workers and repeated module loading remain.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Measure preparation wall time and process count.

tradeoffs.assessment: Transient Python process and module use remains unchanged.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Record peak host RSS during observation.

tradeoffs.assessment: The resume table closes effect replay, but staging and runtime drift still create host stops.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Run crash cuts and benign host-drift fixtures.

tradeoffs.assessment: The current focused test already stops on host runtime-tree drift.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Count qualification refreshes over two host package update cycles.

tradeoffs.assessment: This option changes the least current code.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Verify existing manifests migrate with only schema-field changes.

residualRisks: Benign Python runtime drift still expires the capability.
Ten staged sources and four workers retain partial-state surface.

acceptanceCriteria: Tests and reports do not alter owner digest.
Crash cuts never replay candidate or rollback.
migrationNotes: Keep live execution disabled during migration.
implementationReadiness.rollback: Revert the focused binding changes before capability activation.

options.title: Stable A90 owner package
options.summary: Review one A90-specific package, one observation worker, the existing recovery adapter, and a small no-replay journal table.

evidenceCoverage.rationale: The package owner preserves all device-effect invariants.
One package and worker replace staged-source and process proliferation.
Independent evidence gains an owner-independent lifetime.
Broad host runtime trees no longer define capability identity.
The existing helper remains the exact recovery adapter.

tradeoffs.assessment: Authority is separated by lifetime while device one-shot controls remain exact.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Map every old hostile fixture to the package owner and replay the crash corpus.

tradeoffs.assessment: One observation worker removes repeated interpreter startup.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Compare wall time and process count against the current owner.

tradeoffs.assessment: Fewer simultaneous Python processes should reduce transient RSS.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Measure peak RSS for identical synthetic observations.

tradeoffs.assessment: Fewer staged names and processes reduce partial-state combinations, while the journal table closes replay.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Inject package, worker, bridge, recovery, and publication failures.

tradeoffs.assessment: Candidate data and tests can change without rebuilding capability identity.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Simulate candidate-only and test-only changes and assert owner digest stability.

tradeoffs.assessment: Package generation, schema translation, and worker consolidation require focused changes.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Run old and new H0 validators over the same fixtures before retiring the old owner.

residualRisks: Trusted host package drift below pinned executables is accepted.
TWRP recovery ADB remains an external compatibility dependency.

acceptanceCriteria: Candidate-only and test-only changes preserve owner capability identity.
Exact-one recovery endpoint is required before boot write.
migrationNotes: Retain current hostile checks until equivalent package coverage passes.
implementationReadiness.rollback: Before activation, restore the disabled current owner; after intent, use only the run's boot rollback.

options.title: Static A90 owner binary
options.summary: Replace Python staging, import, bridge, and journal ownership with one compiled A90 binary and narrow recovery adapter.

evidenceCoverage.rationale: A typed binary can encode the one-shot state machine.
Python staging and command subprocesses disappear.
Evidence is external to the binary digest.
Recovery behavior must be retained or reimplemented and revalidated.

tradeoffs.assessment: The executable closure shrinks, but new serial and recovery code can introduce fresh defects.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Differentially test all protocol and journal fixtures against the Python reference.
Benchmark end-to-end H0 preparation and observation.

tradeoffs.assessment: One binary should use fewer runtime objects and processes.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Measure peak RSS and process count.

tradeoffs.assessment: A smaller runtime competes with rewrite risk in mature recovery behavior.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Run prolonged fault-injection and compatibility tests before selection.

tradeoffs.assessment: One binary digest is easy to deploy, but a new toolchain must be qualified.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Build reproducibly on two clean hosts and compare bytes.

tradeoffs.assessment: Serial parsing, recovery sequencing, and journals require a full rewrite and review.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Maintain a staged side-by-side H0 rollout with isolated namespaces.

residualRisks: New implementation defects can affect recovery.
ADB and TWRP remain external dependencies.

migrationNotes: Do not permit both owners to share approval or journal namespaces.
implementationReadiness.rollback: Retain the disabled Python owner until the binary capability is independently qualified.

opportunities.recommendation: Use one stable A90-specific owner package under the current trusted-host and repeated-kernel-experiment constraints; retain the corrected strong closure only if exact host runtime reproducibility is prioritized, and defer a static rewrite until campaign duration justifies it.

openQuestions: Is the exact TWRP ADB serial stable, or must topology plus exact-one arrival bind recovery?
Can the current helper run from one package without changing file-relative behavior?
How many further A90 kernel candidates are expected?
Which host package drift classes should expire capability review?
